extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PD/PIs, senior/key personnel, and other significant contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing NIH-formatted biographical sketches for all senior/key personnel and other significant contributors on NIH grant applications, including content, format, and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must have a biosketch
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with any principal investigators (PIs), include a biographical sketch with research support information for everyone you designate as senior/key personnel or other significant contributors (OSCs). This includes consultants and technical staff with senior/key personnel or OSC designations, even if they are not paid a salary from the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSCs who contribute at least one person month or more effort must be designated as senior/key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH biosketches must conform to a specific format and may not exceed five pages per person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five-page limit includes the table at the top of the first page. Get the NIH Biosketch Format Pages, Instructions, and Samples and use SciENcv to help develop and automatically format the biosketch according to NIH requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All key personnel’s biosketches have a personal statement which must explicitly state how their experience qualifies them for their role on your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't skimp on this key section — the personal statement can be a big factor for the Investigator review criterion. Include relevant education, expertise, and accomplishments. If you have an imminent promotion (e.g., to assistant professor), include the scheduled date in the personal statement and follow rules for Post-Submission Materials to update reviewers if it occurs after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-use: demonstrate ability to execute the Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers check carefully to see whether the PI and others have enough experience, knowledge, skills, and resources necessary to execute the Research Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The personal statement and contributions to science can be big factors in how you rate on the Investigator review criterion. Reviewers will also evaluate whether you have asked for an appropriate number of people, amount of time, and level of expertise to conduct the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe contributions to science
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe your scientific contributions so reviewers can assess your experience when evaluating the scientific contributions in your biosketch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each contribution, you may cite up to four publications or research products that are relevant. If you are not the author of the product, indicate what your role or contribution was. Note that you may mention manuscripts not yet accepted as part of a contribution, but you may cite only published papers to support each contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice for new scientists on contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have limited publications or experience, provide alternative descriptions of contributions appropriate to your situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have one publication, summarize its key finding and importance. If you have no publications yet, describe your efforts on other people's papers and projects (e.g., used a method, provided literature review, cared for research animals). If you have no research or thesis experience yet, you may still describe one contribution about your training to date. You do not have to be an author on publications you reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as research products
rubrics_metrics.description: Research products that may be cited to support contributions include a range of outputs beyond journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: audio or video products, conference proceedings such as meeting abstracts, posters, or other presentations; patents; data and research materials; databases; educational aids or curricula; instruments or equipment; models; protocols; and software or netware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on citations per contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: For each contribution, you may cite up to four publications or research products that are relevant to the contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not the author of the product, indicate your role. While you may reference manuscripts not yet accepted, only published papers may be cited to support each contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on hyperlinks/URLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of hyperlinks and URLs to cite items in the biosketch is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research support section expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight each person's accomplishments in the research support section of the biosketch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include research support information for everyone designated as senior/key personnel or OSCs; use this section to show relevant accomplishments and resources that support the role on the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with other application components
rubrics_metrics.description: Biosketches should be consistent with other parts of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure roles, effort, dates, and descriptions align with the Research Plan, budget, and other application sections to avoid discrepancies that could raise reviewer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project application rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-project applications, each Senior/Key Person, including the PD/PI, is allowed one biosketch for the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual will participate on multiple components, attach the biosketch to any single component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholastic Performance section required for certain applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for certain types of applications must also include the Scholastic Performance section in their biosketch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowships and dissertation research grants (e.g., R36). Consult the Instructions for a Biographical Sketch for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist-style reviewer goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Key items reviewers expect from biosketches (summary checklist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure: personal statement showcases skills; you convince reviewers you are the right person to lead the research; other biosketches convince reviewers that team members can perform needed roles; each person's research support highlights accomplishments; chosen publications reveal skills of the individual and team; biosketches are consistent with other application parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools and resources to prepare biosketch
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NIH-provided format pages, instructions, samples, and tools to prepare compliant biosketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get the NIH Biosketch Format Pages, Instructions, and Samples, review the Instructions for a Biographical Sketch and the Frequently Asked Questions on Biosketches, and use SciENcv to help develop and automatically format the biosketch according to NIH requirements.
